glosses.732.101: When someone dies without a will, the parts of the estate the will does not cover pass to the heirs named in the statute.
glosses.732.502: A will must be signed by the testator at the end, and signed by two witnesses in the testator’s presence.
glosses.732.503: A self-proving affidavit lets the will be admitted without the witnesses testifying later; failing it does not invalidate the will.
glosses.732.401: A homestead cannot be devised away from a surviving spouse or minor child, so it descends as the constitution requires.
glosses.732.201: A surviving spouse who is unhappy with the will can elect a share of the elective estate instead of taking under it.
glosses.732.603: If a beneficiary dies before the testator the gift generally lapses, unless the beneficiary’s descendants take it or the will says otherwise.
glosses.736.0502: A spendthrift clause stops a beneficiary’s creditors from reaching trust distributions before they are paid.
glosses.736.0802: A trustee must act only in the beneficiaries’ interests and must not put the trustee’s own interests first.
